chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from one of our companions—and I do not think him to be anyone but Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī—who said:
It was said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام regarding dough kneaded with impure water: what should be done with it? He said: It should be sold to one who deems eating carrion permissible.

key_terms.الْعَجِينِ: dough prepared for use or consumption
key_terms.الْمَاءِ النَّجِسِ: ritually impure water that renders what it contacts impure
key_terms.كَيْفَ يُصْنَعُ بِهِ: what practical legal action should be taken concerning it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dough kneaded with impure water in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about dough prepared with impure water. Rather than being used by Muslims, it is to be disposed of through sale to those who consider eating carrion permissible, indicating its impermissibility for normal Muslim consumption.
